title: Undecidable prime-factor maps
plain: Show no algorithm can decide, given a and b, whether every orbit of n ↦ n/2 (even) or the largest prime factor of an + b (odd) eventually loops.
math: Prove $\{(a,b)\in\mathbb{N}^2:$ every orbit of $n\mapsto n/2$ ($n$ even), $P(an+b)$ ($n$ odd) is eventually periodic$\}$ is not recursive, or prove it is.
